title: Optimal Kernel Orchestration for Tensor Programs with Korch
problem: Kernel orchestration requires mapping DNN operators to GPU kernel execution on modern hardware. Prior greedy operator fusion approaches miss optimization opportunities in how kernels are orchestrated and scheduled.
motivation: Efficient kernel orchestration is critical for maximizing GPU performance and resource utilization in deep learning workloads.
method: When running deep neural network operations on GPUs, greedy operator fusion combines operations one-by-one without considering how they might be organized together later, missing optimization opportunities. Korch systematically explores different ways to map and schedule groups of operations onto GPU kernels, rather than making locally optimal fusion choices. By considering the full space of orchestration strategies—how kernels should be organized and when they should run—Korch finds execution plans that run faster than greedy fusion would.
key_novelty: Optimal kernel orchestration by exploring the full space of possible mapping and scheduling strategies instead of greedily fusing operators.
contributions: Identifies fundamental limitations of greedy operator fusion in kernel orchestration
Develops optimal orchestration strategies for mapping tensor program operators to GPU kernels
Demonstrates improved GPU utilization through comprehensive kernel mapping optimization
limitations: Specific optimization mechanisms, experimental results, and detailed performance metrics not discussed in abstract.
